learning_objective: 🎯 Enter the modern era of geography! Discover how computers, satellites, and software map the world in ways humans never could.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Geographical Information System (GIS) is a computer system designed to capture, store, manipulate, analyze, manage, and present all types of geographical data.
GIS needs 5 things to work: Hardware (computers), Software (mapping programs), Data (coordinates and attributes), People (to run it), and Procedures (rules for analysis).
Raster data represents the world as a grid of pixels/cells (like a digital photograph). Vector data represents the world using points, lines, and polygons (like a drawn map).
Non-spatial data linked to a spatial location. The map shows a dot (spatial vector data), and the attribute data tells you that dot is 'Delhi, Population 30 Million'.
GIS is used everywhere! From Google Maps giving you directions, to governments planning smart cities, predicting weather, and managing disaster relief.

fun_activity.title: 📍 You Are a GIS System!
fun_activity.instructions: Open Google Maps. Zoom in on your house. You are looking at a mix of Vector data (the lines showing roads) and Raster data (turn on Satellite view to see the pixel images)!

exam_tips: 📌 Be able to clearly distinguish between Raster data format (grid cells/pixels) and Vector data format (points/lines/polygons).
📌 Know the 5 essential components of a GIS system.
📌 Understand how spatial data is linked with attribute data (this is the core power of GIS).
quick_recap: ⭐ A point in vector data is defined by an exact X and Y coordinate.
⭐ Scanned maps and satellite images are common examples of raster data.
⭐ GIS allows analysts to 'layer' different maps on top of each other (e.g., roads over forests over rivers).
